items.reasoning: Ledger entries A1–A3 recorded the landlord's decision and approved Eliza Bennett's quote at £1,370 (no VAT). A4 emailed Eliza that the quote was approved and asked for start dates. A5 told the landlord the approval was recorded and that he would get the dates by 19 May. The start date isn't known yet, so asking for dates and committing to update the landlord is a reasonable way to meet this outcome.
items.evidence: A4: 'the landlord has approved your quote of £1,370 (no VAT)... Please reply with the dates you can start'; A5: 'We'll update you once Eliza confirms dates, by 2025-05-19.'

items.reasoning: The invoice request went in the same email as the new-works instruction. However, it is clearly marked as the invoice for the previous refurb and kept apart from the new job. The landlord is told it will be passed to him for checking, and Remaining work lists it as its own item. It is not mixed into the new works.
items.evidence: A4: 'The landlord has also asked you to resend your invoice from the previous refurb so he can check it.'

items.reasoning: The agent did not create a separate ticket. It did email the landlord asking for the address of the other flat 'so we can log it'. It also listed the leak in Remaining work and Missing information to be logged separately. The leak is not lost, and getting the address is the necessary first step.
items.evidence: A5: 'you mentioned a roof leak at another flat: please send us its address so we can log it'

items.reasoning: Under what is not established, the agent explicitly notes that the roof leak is not logged because there is no address.
items.evidence: 'Roof leak at another property is not logged: no address'

items.reasoning: Every message says £1,370 with no VAT.
The agent kept the leak separate: it says it will be logged separately once the address arrives and is not part of this job.
items.evidence: 'Landlord to supply address of the roof-leak flat, then log separately'

items.reasoning: The only quote approved and instructed was Eliza Bennett's £1,370, which is named and approved.
The quote items were taken from the initial request text, and the agent states 'quote document not seen'. It does not rely on the content of any missing attachment.
items.evidence: record_quote source: 'events 024 and 028 emails; quote document not seen'

grades.overall_note: The agent judged the case well. It recorded the approved quote, instructed the right contractor at the right price and kept the old invoice and the roof leak apart from the new works. One minor weakness is that the invoice request went in the same email as the new-works instruction rather than a separate one.
